speaker: philipcarbullido
text: The Supreme Court of Guam is now in session. Will the clerk please call the case?

speaker: Other
text: This is Supreme Court case number CVA19-019. Guam Police Department, Major Fred M. Chargoloff, petitioner, appellant, versus Government of Guam Retirement Fund, respondent, appellee. Appearing for the respondent appellee is Attorney Vincent C. Camacho. Appearing for the petitioner appellant is Attorney Joshua D. Walsh. The panel consists of Chief Justice F. Philip Carbolito, Associate Justice Robert J. Torres, and Chief Justice Alexandro C. Castro. Attorney Walsh reserves 12 minutes.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: Thank you. Good morning, Attorney Camacho and Attorney Walsh. At this time, Mr. Walsh, you are recognized.

speaker: joshuawalsh
text: Thank you, Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court. When an administrative agency adversely affects the vested property rights of a retirement fund member through a determination that conflicts with the plain reading of a statute and does so without developing a record to stand upon, that decision is due no deference and should be rejected. When a court reviewing an administrative decision also chooses to abandon the plain reading of a statute and does so using its own rationale not previously advanced by the agency, that court decision is in error and must be corrected as well. That is what has occurred here. At the heart of this case is the annuity calculation used to determine the benefit owed to Major Chargoloff, a career public safety official in Maryland. This court has directed that the statutory analysis begins with the statute. So that seems like a good place to start here. That is also the place that the Superior Court started. The calculation that we're discussing is dependent on the definition of average annual salary. That's at 4 GCA 8122. The Superior Court of Guam correctly explained that the plain language of that statute favors the interpretation of Major Chargoloff. That's a finding of the Superior Court that is not on appeal here. The Retirement Fund did not bring an appeal about that conclusion.

speaker: philipcarbullido
text: And Mr. Walsh, Mr. Walsh, isn't this a de novo review? And so regardless, you brought the appeal saying that the Retirement Fund's interpretation is incorrect. And under a de novo review, we get to decide separate and apart from the trial courts and the administrative agency's decisions in order to address the issues that you've raised on appeal.

text: Absolutely, Mr. Chief Justice. I mean, yes, this is a de novo review and this court's view of the law is going to make its way into the opinion of that judge control. The reason that I raised the idea that this was not raised on appeal from the fund, and this also plays into the second point that wasn't raised on appeal by the fund, the Chevron deference determination by the Superior Court. The reason that I raised it is because of the unique sort of situation that we're in here, where the result of an administrative agency was ultimately upheld, but not on the logic from the administrative agency. So, you know, this sort of situation where the administrative agency does not have to bring an appeal because it likes the result, but the rationale for the result isn't the same as the agency's, I think it's worth pointing out. That's what I'm hoping to do here. So, of course, Chief Justice Carbolito, it's a de novo review and you were able to say what the law means in this situation. I think the unique procedural footing here is worth pointing out. And the other reason I think that's worth pointing out is for the benefit of an appellant, like Major Chargelot. We have rules of procedure for this court that allow for cross-appeals, or for cross-firing appeals, for the issues to be briefed, for another round of briefing to address issues that an appellant or an appellee feel need to be addressed. Those weren't accessed here. So, while it is de novo review, I think the interesting fact that the superior court rationale does not match the agency's rationale, but the result was the same, is worth pointing that out. And that's why I offer it.
